## Today

`ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.canShowSystemPrompt` (both
`:app-wear` and `:app-phone`) does read the first-request flag and
then `ActivityCompat.shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale`, exactly as
the gap describes — that helper alone cannot distinguish a granted
permission from a permanently refused one. But nothing calls
`canShowSystemPrompt` on its own: the sole caller is
`ConnectivityPermissionManager.requestAgain`
(`core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/connectivity/ConnectivityPermissionManager.kt`),
shared by both apps, and it already checks `system.isGranted()` first
— returning `Resolved(Granted)` immediately and never reaching
`canShowSystemPrompt`/`openAppSettings` when the permission is already
granted. This is the identical pattern the gap names as the correction
on `SensorPermissionManager.requestAgain`, already present here too.
`ConnectivityPermissionManagerTest` carries a test for this exact
scenario — `requestAgain returns Resolved Granted without opening
settings when the permission is already granted, even if the system
prompt is exhausted` — which passes against the current code. The
redirect-to-settings-when-granted behaviour the gap reports does not
occur.
